data.body:
Measured evidence from CI wall-clock investigation (Gerrit Verified gate) — adds a THIRD partial-clone site this epic should cover, plus hard numbers for the reclaim case.

## Site not yet in file_impact: gerrit-verify.yaml's verify-identity job

file_impact currently lists .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml for the checkout filter. The SAME full-history fetch exists in .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml, job 'verify-identity', step 'Mount the tickets store (FULL history for commit-ancestry era scoping)' — a bare 'git fetch' with a comment explicitly rejecting --depth. (The sibling 'require-ticket' job in the same file already uses --depth=1, so only this one is full.)

## Measured cost (run 30569775555, 2026-07-30)

Job total 7.3m, of which:
  - 6.73m  Mount the tickets store (the fetch)
  - 0.08m  the actual 'rebar verify-identity' invocation
So 92% of the job is the clone. The check itself is ~5 seconds because identity.require_authenticated = false (rebar.toml:105) puts it in advisory mode, which short-circuits all git work at verify_authorship.py:532 before any commit map is built.

## Local measurements of the tickets branch (fetched from the GitHub mirror)

  full fetch          66.2s   1.4 GB   51,575 commits
  --filter=blob:none   3.6s    22 MB
  + worktree add       8.6s    83 MB  (materializes HEAD blobs only)

18x faster, 64x smaller for the fetch; ~12s total end-to-end vs 66s locally (6.73m on a GH runner).

## The stated blocker does NOT apply

The step comment justifies the full fetch as needed for 'merge-base / commit-ancestry scoping against identity.enforce_since'. A blob:none partial clone keeps the COMPLETE commit graph — only blobs are lazy. Verified directly on the partial clone:

  git merge-base --is-ancestor 0cf8c03530d379991933740d9e4d1fa46ce4484a refs/remotes/gh-tickets  -> exit 0

So the era-scoping requirement is fully preserved. Note --depth/shallow would NOT be safe here: _is_enforced (verify_authorship.py:299-319) fails CLOSED on any git error, so a truncated graph turns grandfathered events into enforced ones and produces spurious failures. blob:none avoids that entirely because the graph is intact.

## Why this matters for the reclaim story (0303)

The 1.4 GB / 51,575-commit figure is the direct measurement of the growth 0303 is trying to bound — every ticket event is an auto-commit. Partial clone is the mitigation; it does not shrink the branch. Both are worth doing: blob:none makes CI cheap NOW regardless of how long the reclaim takes to land.

## Caveat on _collect_all under blob:none

In ENFORCED mode (require_authenticated = true) _collect_all reads every active event file at HEAD, which the worktree checkout already materializes — that is the 83 MB above, not a lazy-fetch storm. But the introducing-commit map (authorship.build_introducing_commit_map, a --full-history git log pass) should be re-measured on a partial clone before enforcement is re-flipped, since a name-only log over 51k commits may fault in trees. Not a blocker for landing the filter while the gate is advisory.

Source: CI wall-clock reduction investigation. Not claiming this ticket — filing the evidence.
